note: Simon's PATTERN LIBRARY BUILD PLAN (2026-11-10), in his build order. A library is 'landed' only when all its claims are decided on a real run, its kernels are witness-clean and this page shows it (CLAIMS.md). 'running' means built, gated, live and growing every night, with claims still to decide; 'not landed' means not built.

libraries.name: Document extraction
libraries.what: Built to pull dates, parties, governing law, renewal and notice terms, liability caps and minimum commitments out of contracts, and to flag ten kinds of clause, each answer with the pattern that gave it. It answers only what its patterns have proven so far.
libraries.data: CUAD v1, 510 real commercial contracts (The Atticus Project, CC BY 4.0)
libraries.why: Not landed yet: X1 (beating the cheap method on a fresh final exam) and P4 (the coverage climb) are first decided on night 1 (2026-11-11, 03:00); P2 and P3 only once the keeper switches the paid tier on.

libraries.name: Build patterns
libraries.what: How every kept pattern was built (which proposer, which recipe, what it cost), looked up first the next night so a sibling task starts from what already worked; and Kar's own build checks, kept on Kar's machine.
libraries.data: the libraries' own night records; Kar's build retrospectives (private, local only)
libraries.why: Not landed yet: its records and Kar's build checks are kept (B1, B2), but the fall in spend per kept pattern (P3) needs weeks of nights that used the paid tier.

libraries.name: Finance and accounting (receipts)
libraries.what: Built to read a receipt's line items, subtotal, tax, service charge, discount, total, cash and change, each answer with the pattern that gave it, and then to check them against each other by arithmetic (items to subtotal, subtotal plus tax to total, cash less change to total): reconciled, flagged or unchecked. It answers only what its patterns have proven so far. Dates, suppliers and payment terms are not in its data, so it does not read them.
libraries.why: Running, not landed: F1, F2, P4 (the coverage climb), R2 and R3 are decided on the nights after its fresh night 0 (seal 4 re-ran it under an exam order that shuffles; the first two nights are kept as void); P2 and P3 only once the keeper switches the paid tier on. R0 (the check tested on the experts' own receipts) is decided.
libraries.data: CORD v2, 1,000 real Indonesian receipts (NAVER CLOVA, CC BY 4.0); text and labels only, never the images

libraries.name: Triage and routing (customer messages)
libraries.what: Built to send a customer's message to the right one of 77 banking teams, naming any other team that also matched, and to flag it when the customer wants a human or something was lost or stolen; each answer with the pattern that gave it. It answers only what its patterns have proven so far; a message with no flag goes to the normal queue, never called safe.
libraries.why: Running, not landed: T1 (beating the cheap method on a fresh final exam) and P4 (the climb) are decided on the nights after night 0; triage has no proven pattern yet. It runs on the free proposers only, so the paid-tier claims cannot arise. Its first nights, run under an exam order that did not shuffle, are kept as void (seal 4).
libraries.data: Banking77 (13,083 messages, 77 intents) and NLU++ (3,080 messages, with "wants a human" and "lost or stolen" labels), by PolyAI, CC BY 4.0

libraries.name: Sales and outreach
libraries.what: What converts, follow-up structure, lead qualification, measured by whether it converted.
libraries.why: Not built yet: it needs real outcome data, which the estate does not have in volume.

libraries.name: Novel angles
libraries.what: Question a requirement, find what to delete, cross one domain's reasoning with another.

libraries.name: Compression and stacked light
libraries.what: Each layer of how the estate's codec folds, as a pattern.
